agree.reason: The shrinking-ads framing, the modest required pace, and the June checkpoint with a fallback to sponsorships would persuade most of the board, but the ad-background members' main question, why not run both, is left as a blank placeholder.

honest.reason: The memo doesn't claim outright that membership will replace ads within a year as the brief asked; it treats the other newsroom's 40% as illustration rather than prediction, and every figure traces to the brief, though it quietly assumes the 212 pilot members carry over.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures all check out: the 36% drop and roughly 20% a year, the $20,352 annualised pilot revenue, 35 a week against 13 needed, 875 members to replace $84k, 700 members to match the projected 2027 ads, and $52k collected in 2027 against $67k; each is framed favourably but accurately.

right_comparison.reason: It correctly compares membership with a declining ad line rather than a flat $84k, though it may be a year off: if $84k was 2025, the trend puts 2027 nearer $54k than $67k, so the comparison is conservative.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint names a date (June 30, 2027), a target (540 members), a trigger (fewer than 450), and a consequence (options including sponsorships at the July meeting), all of which the board can check.

objections.reason: It addresses the revenue gap, churn and slowing sign-ups, and the 11-year colleague, but the 'why stop rather than run both' argument and the source for the $15k gap are left blank, so the sceptical members' key objections aren't yet answered.

fit.reason: It is a one-page board memo with a clear decision request and recommendation, though several bracketed placeholders still need filling in.
